features.optics-sfp-plus: Table 1-3 Supported SFP+ Modules (PDF p12, printed 1-10), the row listing this model: SFP-10G-LR=, SFP-10G-SR=, SFP-10G-LRM=, and SFP-H10GB-CU1M=, -CU3M= and -CU5M= twinax cables.
features.sfp-plus-slots: 2 SFP+ module slots (numbered 25 and 26 here; the guide states no numbers for this model), 10 Gigabit; the SFP+ slots also take 1 Gigabit SFP modules
features.stacking: FlexStack, optional C2960S-STACK module in the rear slot

management.console: USB mini-Type B and RJ-45; the USB port has priority when both are connected (Table 1-10)

physical.weight-note: 12.5 lb (5.66 kg), spec Table 1-2 row Catalyst 2960S-24PD-L

power.power-input-ac: 100 to 240 VAC (autoranging), 5 to 2 A, 50 to 60 Hz

ac.description: The switch as it runs: the built-in AC supply and the blank cover over the FlexStack module slot. The C2960S-STACK module is optional (PDF p21, printed 1-19) and is not seated here.

with-flexstack-module.description: The same switch with the optional C2960S-STACK FlexStack module fitted in place of the blank cover (PDF p31, printed 1-7). Not a SKU: the stack kit is ordered separately (PDF p29, printed 1-5).

ws-c2960s-24pd-l.description: WS-C2960S-24PD-L, the model's only SKU (Table 1-1, LAN Base, PoE budget 370 W). It seats the blank cover in the FlexStack slot: the stack kit is a separate, optional part (PDF p21, printed 1-19) and the cover is removed only to fit the module (PDF p31).

description: 24x 10/100/1000 PoE+ RJ-45 (370 W PoE budget) and 2x SFP+ uplink 1RU stackable access switch running LAN Base. The front carries the mode button and switch lamps at the left, two blocks of twelve jacks in two rows at the right of the face, then the USB Type A port, the USB mini-Type B and RJ-45 console ports, the Ethernet management port and the two SFP+ slots. The rear carries the FlexStack module slot with its blank cover, the fan exhaust, the RPS connector and the AC inlet of the built-in supply. Ports number 1-24 and run DOWN each column - odd on the top row, even beneath it. The SFP+ pair follows the copper ports.

gaps.wanted: A flat drawing of the lid, the underside and the two side walls. The guide's figures show the lid and one side isometrically (bracket screw holes and slots on the side); none can be measured. Each carries an `empty:` sentence saying where I looked.

The RPS connector is the part cisco/rps2300-connector@2, drawn open where the photograph puts it. The part draws the plate, its two screw holes, the shroud with its dark top edge, the housing and the two rows of eleven cavities with a contact in each; it draws the cells with their chamfered lower corners and does not draw the slot in the screws, which the photograph shows at about one pixel. The rating strip stays chassis art. The guide says the cover (two Phillips pan-head screws, Figure 1-15) goes on when no RPS is connected.

This model's own rear in colour. The only held rear in colour with the FlexStack slot is the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L, whose plain plate reads #3f4447 and whose fitted module's plain frame reads #3f565d; the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-24TS-L rear (no FlexStack slot, read for colour only) reads #404145. The drawn #404040 is within 7 levels of 255 of each. The guide's own drawing of the rear (Figure 1-10, PDF p19, printed 1-17) is pale grey (#d4d6d8) and shades one finish by the light on each face, so it conflicts with the photographs; the guide gives no housing colour. The rear is drawn charcoal, a stand-in that the owner may accept or replace. The front is not in doubt: the teal edge, charcoal panel and white console surround are what the four 2960-S stencils agree on, and Figure 1-1 draws the same scheme.

Cisco's logo is never drawn (the region `logo-zone` stays). The corner marks 1X, 11X, 2X, 12X and so on at the corners of each block read clearly on the stencil but sit where the jack part's box begins: each mark's inner 0.6 to 1.0 mm lies under the part, so a mark would be half hidden and is not drawn.

The ETSI mounting bracket, printed "700-19781XX" (PDF p34, printed 1-10). Its revision digits are not read, and the guide gives no contents or install steps beyond Figure 1-10, so no kit contract is written.
The numbers of the two SFP+ slots on this 24-port model. The guide says "Module slot numbers are 49 and 50" under the 48-port figure only. They are numbered 25 and 26 here, after the copper ports.
A square-on photograph of this model's front. The only flat face is community art; every position is read from it at 11.3 px per mm.
The Mode button is drawn as plain panel art. No library part is a flush push button of this shape.

The rating label text beside the inlet. The photograph shows another model's label ("100-240V~ 8-4A") and the guide's drawing "12-6A", and this model's row of Table 1-2 reads 5 to 2 A, so none is carried.

A `common/led-arrow-sm` skin whose off fill is the stencil's solid light grey (#808080: 120 px, box (520,96,535,104) of a port arrow and 155 px, box (4660,118,4676,128) of the console arrow; each arrow 2.38 x 2.12 mm) without the dark fill and the #5b6167 edge. The part is on `main` and its skin is not edited, and a lamp's colour in the static drawing is the part's own (a lamp state paints only when a state is set), so each lamp keeps its dark triangle; a light grey triangle of the stencil's size is drawn under it, which leaves a light rim of about 0.25 mm, and the black disc the punched lamp opening drew is covered in the panel's colour. The three lamps by the console and management jacks are arrows too (Figure 1-9, PDF p18, printed 1-16, "Console LEDs": 1 USB console LED, 2 RJ-45 console LED; Table 1-10 gives their colours): they were round dots and are arrow lamps now, down for the USB console LED, right for the RJ-45 console LED (the up skin turned 90 degrees: a lamp, not a connector) and up under the management jack.

A white or silver body for the RJ-45 part. The console jack, the management jack and the 48 jack-block jacks are `std/rj45-ganged@2`, whose only skin paints a near-black body with light grey shoulders. The stencil draws the console and management jacks on a white plate (#efefef, 10086 px of each, boxes (4782,86,4959,226) and (4998,86,5175,226)) round a dark opening, so a plate of that colour and outline (15.6 x 12.34 mm) is drawn under each of the two jacks and the part keeps its own body. On the 48 block jacks the stencil draws charcoal bodies with white shoulders, where the render has near-black bodies with light grey shoulders; left: the part's skin. Request: an `std/rj45` skin with a white body or white shoulders. The latch stays up and the contacts down, as the stencil shows them.

A USB-A skin with a silver interior and the tongue at the left, as the stencil shows. `std/usb-a@1` is placed with `skin: usb2` and rotated 90 degrees, and draws a black opening (#17191c) with a pale tongue (#d5d9de) to the right of the middle of the vertical opening; the stencil draws a silver-grey shell with the tongue at the left. Neither skin of the part draws a silver interior (`default` draws a blue tongue, `usb2` a white one, in the same place), so the part stays as it is. The only way to bring the tongue to the left with this skin is a 270 degree turn of the placed part, which is a rotation and is the owner's to decide. Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is too small at this port to say more. The shell around the part is drawn silver (#7b7b7b).

A mini-B skin with the five contacts in the lower half of the opening. `std/mini-usb@1` draws the flat edge at the top, bevelled corners at the bottom and the five contacts (#7a8087) in the upper half; the stencil has the same flat edge and bevel and the contacts in the lower half. The stencil is the only source of the contact side: Figure 1-5 (USB Mini-Type B Port, PDF p9, printed 1-7) draws a mini-B port with the bevelled corners at the top and contacts both on its tongue and in a row below it, which does not settle the side for this connector as it is mounted, and Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is too small. The part's skin is not edited and the connector is not turned: turning it would put the bevel on top, and a rotation after merge is a major version.

A version of the SFP+ cage part with the stencil's silver frame (#cfcfcf, 1423 px of each cage), its two clips on the right side (#bdbdbd with black edges), its two small squares near the top (#707070), its gold contacts at the lower left and its pull tab inside the opening. The part's own skin paints a grey collar (#9aa0a8) round a dark opening and its skin is not edited here. Drawn outside or under the part's box: the silver as the surround the part leaves visible (about 0.5 mm each side), the black projection at each cage's foot (#000000, 861 px, box (4570,427,4652,441)), the silver pull tab (#c1c5cb, 240 px, box (4588,416,4636,421); all but about 0.2 mm of it lies under the part's box and is hidden) and the white numeral tab under each cage (#f2f2f2, 2112 px, box (4570,450,4652,477)) with its numeral in #595959 (70 px, box (4600,456,4624,474)). Not drawn: the clips, the squares and the gold contacts, because they lie inside the cage's own opening and would paint over the part's skin. Request: `std/sfp` with the clips, squares, contacts and pull tab in its opening.

The "MGMT" and "BASET" legend right of the management jack. The stencil prints it vertically in yellow (#ffff99, 341 px, box (5190,95,5215,212)): the letters M, G, M, T, then a gap, then B, A, S, E, T, one above the other and upright, each 0.78 mm tall, 10.3 mm in all (it reads "BASET", with no hyphen, at 6x). A legend 0.78 mm tall is under the 1.5 mm font size the library's legend test asks for, so it is not drawn. Wanted: a photograph or a dimensioned front that gives the legend at a size that reads.

A dimensioned view of this model's rear. The NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L (3.41 px per mm) shows these things that the render does not, each looked at at 4x: the chassis' own diagonal edge at the far right, running from about (422.6, 18) up to (443.7, 1.5) mm with two small steps below it, which is the chassis outline and is not drawn over the face; two small oval tabs above and below the AC inlet, about 9 x 3 mm at (386 to 396, 3 to 6) and (386 to 396, 33 to 36) mm, whose interior (#323637, 110 px, box (1322,12,1344,17)) is 5 levels of 255 from the plate round it (#373b3e, 200 px, box (1360,12,1400,17)), too faint for an outline to be placed, so they are not drawn; faint rectangular outline marks stamped in the rear plate between the module and the fan and beside the RPS plate; a small round hole at the left of the fan, near (149.6, 28.7) mm; a small dark notch in the RPS plate's left edge, near (285 to 288, 25 to 33) mm; and the AC inlet's three pins, which are light grey blocks in the render and dark pockets with a small light mark in the photograph. All are drawn from one model's photograph and none from the guide, whose Figure 1-10 (PDF p19, printed 1-17) is too small to show them.

mgmt.mixed: the RJ-45 console port and the 10/100/1000 Ethernet management port at the right of the front: two jobs, one purpose, reaching the switch when the data plane cannot

mode-leds.description: the five port-mode lamps; the one lit says what each port lamp shows (Table 1-7)

name: ws-c2960s-24pd

airflow.note: The guide names a fan exhaust on the rear panel, counts no fans and gives no direction; no airflow is set and no fan redundancy is claimed.

colour.note: Front: the NetBox stencil of this model (cisco-ws-c2960s-24pd-l.front.png, 5475 x 503 px) is read for colour, a community artist's flat palette, not a reading of the metal: the bezel #255e6d (median of 7000 px, box (700,6,1200,20) of a 5475 x 503 px stencil; the lower edge, box (700,482,1200,497), reads the same), the charcoal panel #404040 (box (435,30,480,110)), the Mode button #255e6d (box (330,435,385,460)) and the console surround #bbd5d8 (box (4800,70,4850,90)); the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L, -48TD-L, -24PD-L and -24TD-L stencils give the same medians in every box. Figure 1-1 (PDF p4, printed 1-2), Cisco's own colour drawing of the 48FPD-L, draws the same scheme (a dark teal front edge round a charcoal panel, yellow frames round the jack blocks) and is the guide's own evidence that the teal is Cisco's finish. So `chassis.color` is #404040 and the teal edge, the console surround and the yellow frames are drawn; every figure is `estimated`. Rear: The rear is drawn in the chassis colour #404040. The only rear in colour with the FlexStack slot is the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-48LPD-L (cisco- ws-c2960s-48lpd-l.rear.png, 1516 x 150 px), whose plain plate reads #3f4447 (median of 2000 px, box (440,15,520,40)) and whose fitted module's frame reads #3f565d (box (230,137,330,142)); the NetBox photograph of the WS-C2960S-24TS-L rear (cisco-ws-c2960s-24ts-l.rear.png, 1102 x 97 px, a model with no FlexStack slot, read for colour only) reads #404145 (box (520,8,590,24)). The drawn #404040 is within 7 levels of 255 of each. Figure 1-10 (PDF p19, printed 1-17) draws the rear pale grey (#d4d6d8, box (330,150,430,185) of the converted figure), shaded by the light on each face; the two photographs and the figure disagree, so the photographs' charcoal is kept and the gap `faceplate- colour` says so.

console.note: Figure 1-1 callouts 5 and 6 and "Management Ports" (Figure 1-5, PDF p9): the USB mini-Type B console port and the RJ-45 console port are one console, and the USB port has priority when both are cabled (Table 1-10). The management port is its own (callout 7).

controls-and-lamps.note: The eight switch lamps (SYST, RPS, MSTR, STAT, DPLX, SPED, STCK, PoE) stand in a column at 7.1 mm, pitched 2.53 mm, the Mode button below them (Figure 1-7, PDF p13, printed 1-11; the PoE lamp is "only on switch models that support PoE", which this one does). Port lamps are the two small arrows above each column pair, up for the upper port and down for the lower; their meaning depends on the selected mode (Table 1-9). The arrows by the console jacks are the USB and RJ-45 console lamps (Table 1-10, PDF p18, printed 1-16).

ears-and-kits.note: Figure 1-12 (PDF p36, printed 1-12) "Attaching Brackets for 19-inch Racks": front-mounting, mid-mounting and rear-mounting positions, with number-8 Phillips flat-head screws (48-0655-01); Figure 1-13 (PDF p37, printed 1-13): number-12 Phillips pan-head screws (48-0523-01) for the rack and a black Phillips machine screw (48-0654-01) for the cable guide. The text says four screws attach each bracket's long side to the switch. The 19-inch brackets are in the box, so they are not a kit. No position is dimensioned, so none carries an `at`. The ETSI bracket is printed "700-19781XX" (PDF p34, printed 1-10), with its revision digits unread: it is a gap and not a kit.

front-console-end.note: The shapes at the console end are read from the NetBox front elevations of the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L, -48TD-L, -24PD-L and -24TD-L (cisco-ws-c2960s-<model>-l.front.png, 5475 x 503 px, 11.345 px per mm, the chassis starting 216 px in, so one pixel is 0.09 mm). The four agree on every shape here. A model whose own stencil is another product is read from them. The legend band's left end slopes from (384.2, 2.1) to (394.5, 4.6) mm: the first teal pixel of each row runs from 4584 to 4683 px over rows 26 to 50. The dark panel's top-right corner is rounded at about 2.2 mm: the teal ends at 5191 px in row 53 and at 5213 px from row 77. The console surround stops at 24.42 mm under the mini-B jack and at 21.24 mm under the RJ-45 jack, with the step at 402.1 mm, so the surround and its dark panel are two rectangles each, and the port lamp below stands on the panel. The stencil rounds the inside of the step by about 0.9 mm and it is drawn square here. The mini-B's lower corners show the surround's teal in the stencil, so two teal triangles, 0.8 by 1.2 mm, cover the hole's black beside the part's bevels.

front-plates.note: The ring, channel, silver plate and bar round each block of jacks, the yellow number tags above them and the yellow tick band under them, the console and management jack plates, the USB shell, the SFP+ frames with their pull tabs and numeral tabs, the Mode button's rim, the arrow fills and the USB symbol are placed as the WS-C2960S-48FPD-L stencil gives them (cisco-ws-c2960s-48fpd-l.front.png, 11.345 px per mm, the chassis starting 216 px in), which the 24PD-L stencil matches in layout and in every colour sampled above. The stencil is a community artist's flat render and these are that artist's palette; no photograph from Cisco of the front is held. The yellow outline stays round the white ring because the figure is isometric and too small to tell a ring from a frame.

gate-1-front.note: The front is read from the NetBox front elevation of the WS-C2960S-24PD-L, checked against the guide first. Its aspect is 5475 / 503 = 10.88 against 10.86 for the 19-inch ear-to-ear width, so it is read at 11.345 px per mm with the chassis starting 216 px (19.05 mm) in. It shows 24 jacks in two blocks of twelve in two rows, as Table 1-1 says, at the right of the face with the left of the panel plain, eight switch lamps including PoE, the USB Type A, mini-B, RJ-45 console, management and two SFP+ slots. The two blocks sit where blocks 3 and 4 of cisco/ws-c2960s-48fpd stand (the first jack 202.9 mm from the chassis side, read by eye against the same stencil family), and that device's positions are used for the jacks and the right-hand cluster. Every position is `estimated`; the image is community art, not Cisco's.

inlet.note: The inlet is an IEC C14 appliance inlet, read from Figures 1-10 and 1-11 (a three-pin keyed inlet with a rating label beside it). The guide does not name the connector type; it says "Use the supplied AC power cord" (PWR-CLP=, PDF p42, printed 1-18). Position: this model shares the PoE rear with the 48FPD-L and 48LPD-L (the serial-number figure, Figure 1-1 of the appendix, PDF p55, names all three), so cisco/ws-c2960s-48fpd's position, read from the NetBox 48LPD-L rear photograph (3.41 px per mm), is used.

jacks.note: Row 1 starts 11.72 mm down the face and row 2 at 26.71, 15.0 apart; the first jack at 202.86 mm from the chassis side and the blocks 89.4 mm apart (6 x 13.97 plus a 5.58 gutter), as on the 48FPD-L. Upper-row jacks take the 180-degree rotation the 4948E's upper row takes.

legend.note: The legend "Catalyst 2960-S Series PoE+ 10G" is printed on the NetBox stencil's face. Figure 1-1 shows only "2960-S" under the console callout, so the full text is the stencil's, which is community art, not this model's own document; it is carried as `estimated`.

lifecycle.note: No lifecycle date is carried. The end-of-sale notices are not held; only titles and list dates would be, and this model's is not among them.

numbering.note: Ports run left to right from the far left, port 1 above port 2 in each pair (the note under Figure 1-3, PDF p5, printed 1-3, which is written for the 48-port models). The stencil prints 1 to 24 above the jacks. The guide states the module slot numbers (49 and 50) only for the 48-port models; this model's slots are unnumbered there, so they are numbered 25 and 26 after the copper ports and the number is a gap. The stencil prints 1 and 2 under the slots. Interface names are in the community NetBox device type only: GigabitEthernet1/0/1 to 1/0/24, the SFP+ slots and FastEthernet0 for the management port.

power.note: Spec Table 1-2, row Catalyst 2960S-24PD-L: AC input 100 to 240 VAC autoranging, 5 to 2 A, 50 to 60 Hz; DC input for the RPS 2300 +12 V @3 A and -52 V @8 A; power consumption 84 W, 286 BTUs per hour (footnote 1: the power consumed internally by the switch at 120 VAC, 60 Hz); power rating 0.46 KVA. The PoE budget is 370 W (Table 1-1; "PoE+", 30 W per port maximum, 370-W switch maximum, spec Table 1-2). The supply is built in: "The switch is powered through the internal power supply" (AC Power Connector, PDF p22, printed 1-20), so it is part of the chassis and not a bay.

rear.note: The rear is the stacking models' common rear (Figure 1-10, with the RPS connector: callouts 1 FlexStack module slot and cover, 2 fan exhaust, 3 RPS connector, 4 AC power connector). Positions come from the NetBox 48LPD-L rear photograph (3.41 px per mm along its width), the PoE models' rear; the serial-number figure groups this model with the 48-port PoE models. It shows a C2960S-STACK module fitted; this device shows the blank cover (the module is optional: "FlexStack Ports", PDF p21, printed 1-19) and takes the module as a configuration. Spec Table 1-2 lists a DC input for the RPS 2300 for this model, so the RPS connector is present. The guide says "If you are not using an RPS with your switch, use the two Phillips pan-head screws to attach the RPS connector cover" (Figure 1-15, PDF p39, printed 1-15), so the connector is drawn open, as the photograph shows it. It is the part cisco/rps2300-connector@2 (interface `cisco-rps2300`), seated at the plate's place; the rating strip stays chassis art. Measured on the photograph at 3.41 px per mm: a metal plate 72.8 x 22.6 mm at (285.0, 21.4) with a raised rating strip above it (49.2 x 3.8 mm at 297.7, 17.9), a black shroud 48.2 x 11.3 mm at (298.4, 24.0) holding a cream housing 46.9 x 9.7 mm, and in it two rows of eleven cavities on a 4.17 mm pitch, with a screw hole at each end of the plate. Eleven across is what the serial-number figures draw (PDF p55-56, printed 1-5 to 1-6); Figure 1-10 draws seven in a smaller figure, and the photograph and the larger figures are followed. The warning label above the plate ("DC inputs for remote power supply specified in manual", with a triangle) is printed on the metal at (294.0, 5.9), 45.2 x 9.7 mm and is drawn as the photograph prints it; the rating strip over the pins and the rating plate beside the inlet (32.7 x 13.4 mm at (351.0, 6.1)) are drawn blank, because the figures the photograph prints match none of this model's own row of the spec tables (see the gap `rear-label-text`). The inlet sits in a moulded black surround 29.3 x 22.5 mm at (387.6, 8.3). The fan exhaust is a honeycomb of hexagons about 9.7 x 8.5 mm on an 8.8 mm column pitch (21 cells, flat-topped), drawn with the library's `vent` pattern scaled by 2.0 with `pattern-pitch` to that pitch over a plate in the web's colour (the photograph's web reads #404345, box (540,44,705,140), the holes #040507), with the two light cut edges above and below the field (#b9bcba, box (533,40,712,46)). Four pan-head screws, 6.8 mm across, stand at 7.3, 111.4, 274.2 and 436.4 mm along and 28.7 mm down; the first is on the module's flange and is drawn with the cover. The FlexStack slot is the fitted module's stepped frame (see the blank cover's contract). The faint stamped corner marks round the fan and one small drilled hole are not drawn.

sources.note: Catalyst 2960-S Switch Hardware Installation Guide, OL-19732-04, 82 pages (the PDF prints its number and no date; Cisco URL https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/td/docs/switches/lan/catalyst2960/hardware/installation/guide_stack/2960SHIG.pdf). Pages below are PDF pages with the printed page after them. Table 1-1 (PDF p3-4, printed 1-1 to 1-2) lists the model; the appendix's Table 1-2 (PDF p62-63, printed 1-2 to 1-3) gives this model's row; Figure 1-10 "Catalyst 2960-S Switch Rear Panel with Stacking Module Slot and RPS connector" (PDF p19, printed 1-17) is the rear of the stacking models. The guide draws no front of this model: Figure 1-1 "Catalyst 2960S-48FPD-L Front Panel" (PDF p4, printed 1-2) is a 48-port sibling's. Community NetBox (second opinion only, not Cisco's): the WS-C2960S-24PD-L device type and its front elevation, a flat stencil render. No data sheet, no vendor 3D model, no photograph and no rear elevation of this model is held. The pages were read through the PDF's text layer and the converted figures were viewed.
